author: NorthEast News Desk
body: England completed a 3-0 Test-series sweep of Pakistan with an eight-wicket victory at Edgbaston, reaching a target of 130 behind unbeaten half-centuries from captain Joe Root and Jordan Cox. Root finished on 62 and Cox on 59 as the hosts closed out the final match after an early wobble in the chase.

Pakistan briefly created pressure with two quick wickets and nearly dismissed Root when he was bowled on a delivery ruled a no-ball. Root and Cox then settled the innings and carried England to the result without another loss. Pakistan had forced England to bat again after a resilient second innings led by debutant Razaullah, who struck 81 from the lower order.

The sweep gave England its first Test-series victory in 19 months and a successful return to captaincy for Root following Ben Stokes’ retirement. England’s bowlers had controlled much of the series, with Ollie Robinson taking 21 wickets. The result offers momentum before a more demanding tour of South Africa, while Pakistan leaves the series looking for greater stability after personnel and coaching changes during a difficult run of results.
dek: Unbeaten half-centuries from Joe Root and Jordan Cox completed an eight-wicket win at Edgbaston and England’s first Test-series victory in 19 months.
headline: Root guides England to 3-0 Test sweep of Pakistan
